title: PR pipeline config
description: Schema for a repository's PR pipeline config: which activities run in which lane slots, in what order, and how far merge authority reaches. Lane and activity names are checked against the standards github-actions-conventions vocabulary by the config reader, not here. Contract: docs/conventions/pr-pipeline/README.md.

version.description: Contract major version. CHANGELOG.md beside this schema records each version.

extends.description: Org defaults this file layers on. Deferred: the grammar is not settled, and the config reader rejects any value.

activities.description: Each activity, defined once and referenced by key from lane slots and composite children.

lanes.description: One section per lane, keyed by the lane's workflow file stem.

loop.description: Caps that end review and fix loops. One per-PR counter, shared by every lane.

review-rounds.description: Full review rounds before reviews narrow to high severity only.

no-progress.description: Lane runs in a row that change nothing before the PR escalates to needs-human.

dependency-review-rounds.description: review-dependency rounds on one Dependabot PR before the next one escalates to needs-human.

fix-ci-rounds.description: fix-ci commits the lanes App pushed to one PR before the next fix-ci run escalates to needs-human, before any model turn.

limits.description: When the lanes restart work the usage limit stopped, and when they stop restarting it. Durations are whole hours.

fallback-reset.description: Hours after a limit stop that names no reset time before its limit is taken to have reset.

reset-clamp-min.description: Fewest hours after a limit stop before a restart, whatever reset the stop names.

reset-clamp-max.description: Most hours after a limit stop before a restart, whatever reset the stop names.

restarts-per-run.description: Issues one work-unblock sweep restarts or re-fires.

limit-stops-per-head.description: Limit stops on one PR head after which the pr-unblock dispatchers stop dispatching it again; also the failed resolve-conflicts runs, and the failed or not-applicable fix-ci runs across base moves, one head gets.

limit-stops-per-issue.description: Limit stops since a person last added agent-ready after which work-unblock hands the issue to a person.

wip-cap.description: The issue lane's WIP cap when the lane merge rate cannot be read; otherwise wip.target-lead-time-hours sets it.

worker-job-ceiling.description: Jobs an issue run may roll over into (stops at a job's time limit that committed new work) since a listed human last added agent-ready; the next such stop hands the issue to a person.

fix-ci-per-run.description: fix-ci dispatches one pr-unblock-dispatch run sends at most.

fix-ci-restarts.description: Further fix-ci dispatches on one PR head after its first fix-ci run ended in failure.

fix-docs-per-run.description: fix-docs dispatches one pr-unblock-dispatch run sends at most.

admission-factor.description: Share of the issue lane's merge rate (lanes App PRs merged per hour over wip.merge-rate-window-hours) admitted per hour. The queued cap is the larger of this share and admission-min-per-hour, times wip.merge-rate-window-hours.

admission-min-per-hour.description: Admissions per hour the queued cap never falls below: it is at least this rate times wip.merge-rate-window-hours, so a day with no lane merges cannot hold admissions shut. 0 removes the floor.

wip.description: The issue lane's WIP cap from the lane merge rate, and the buffer for held lane PRs. Contract: README.md, WIP cap.

target-lead-time-hours.description: Target open-to-merge hours. The WIP cap is the lane merge rate per hour times this, rounded up, at least min-cap.

min-cap.description: Floor under the computed WIP cap, so a day with few merges cannot shrink the cap until the lane stalls.

merge-rate-window-hours.description: Rolling window over which merged and opened lane PRs are counted.

opened-to-merged-ratio.description: Lane PRs opened in the window may reach at most this share of lane PRs merged in it.

held-cap.description: Open held lane PRs at or above which the held buffer is over its cap; on or after pause-from the issue lane pauses there.

held-alarm-hours.description: Age in hours past which a held lane PR raises the alarm.

pause-from.description: UTC date (or date-time) from which the issue lane pauses while over the WIP cap or the held cap. Empty: it never pauses, it only alerts.

red-main.description: The red-main revert rule: when a confirmed red full run on main is pinned to one merge, and which limits hold the bot's revert back. Contract: README.md, Red main.

dry-run.description: true: report the culprit, the evidence runs and the revert the bot would open, and write nothing else.

daily-cap.description: Auto-reverts the bot opens in any 24 hours, counting dry-run decisions; 0 sends every culprit to a person.

max-culprit-age-hours.description: Hours since the culprit merged past which it goes to a person instead of an auto-revert.

confirm-wait-minutes.description: Minutes the report waits for the one re-run of a red full run to finish; a run with no finished re-run is not confirmed red.

remedy.description: How a pinned culprit is repaired. rollback: the revert rule decides who reverts it. fail-forward: no revert is planned, and a person or a fix pull request repairs main.

adoption.description: The lanes adopt every trusted-actor-list account's non-draft pull requests, a person's once idle: fix-ci fixes a failed ci-status, and pr-merge merges under its usual gates. Absent: none. Contract: README.md, Adoption.

idle-hours.description: Hours both a person's pull request (its last update) and its head commit (its committer date) must be unchanged before it is adopted. Absent: nothing is adopted.

spec-from-body-apps.description: App account ids whose pull request bodies a script writes: an adopted one that closes no issue is judged against its title and body, as a person's is. Any other App needs a closing issue a trusted person wrote.

branch-cleanup.description: The scheduled branch cleanup: how many branches it deletes in one run. Contract: README.md, Branch cleanup.

max-deletes-per-run.description: Branches one run deletes at most; the rest wait for the next run. 0 deletes none.

stage.description: Pipeline stage. Order and meaning: README.md, Stages.

predicate.description: When the activity applies. Every listed key must match; an absent key matches anything.

labels-absent.description: Matches only when none of these labels is on the PR. A miss skips with awaiting-human.

mergeable.description: The PR's mergeability at the gated head. Unknown mergeability never matches and skips with prerequisite-missing.

draft.description: Whether the PR is a draft.

admission.description: Which `work-class:` labels an issues lane admits: an issue carrying a `work-class:` label outside `classes` is refused, even beside a listed one; otherwise it is admitted by a listed class label. Work-class labels match in any casing or spacing, and labels are read when the run starts. With no `admission`, no work-class label is read.

skip-reason.description: The one reason a skipped activity's neutral check carries. Not used by the config file; the runner and check-run reporter validate reasons against it. Meaning: README.md, Outputs and skips.

activity.description: A leaf runs one skill or script; a composite groups other activities.

composite.description: Activities run as one group. It declares no effect: the config reader applies lane rules to each of its leaves, and each leaf runs, is granted and reports on its own.

children.description: Leaf activities, in the order and under the rules of a lane's slots.

applies-when.description: Gates every child; each leaf's own predicate must also match.

edit-runner.description: Only the runner that stages a skill's edit tools grants checks, self-checks, verify-scripts and web-access: the write runner, or the read runner for a skill with applied-by.patch and no prepare: ci-context. Anywhere else they would do nothing, so they are refused.

prepare.description: What the runner does around the activity (README.md, Activities; pr-run-activity.md, the prepare sections). apply-patch is the one mode for a script, a mutate-branch one; the others run around a skill. ci-context needs effect read and hands its change on as a patch; merge-base, review-threads and dependency-review need an effect other than read unless their activity hands its change on as a patch, review-threads with effect read also hands on its replies (applied-by.feedback-replies), and dependency-review with effect read its verdict (applied-by.dependency-verdict). ci-context: download the failing-check context file a base job wrote, check its SHA-256 and head, make it read-only and name it to the skill, which also gets Bash, Edit and Write. apply-patch: check the patch artifact a producer left (one patch.diff with its SHA-256, on the head it worked on), apply it to the gated head, and push it as one commit without force; patch-rules.json registers the rules each producer's patch is to be held to (README.md, Patch rules). merge-base: merge the base tip without committing before the skill, then commit with the gated head and the base tip as parents (with effect read, a base job of the caller merges first and decides, the read runner merges the same base again and hands the skill's resolutions on as a patch measured from the conflict tree, and a prepare: apply-patch script commits the merge). review-threads: before any model turn, keep the PR's unresolved reviewer-bot threads on a reviewed head and escalate on a .github/** diff or the round cap (on the read runner, a base job of the caller does this and the runner checks its thread file); give the skill the review-thread tool; after it, upload the replies it recorded for a script job to validate and post. dependency-review: before any model turn, skip a PR Dependabot did not open or one sorted auto, and escalate on the round cap (on the read runner, a base job of the caller does this and the runner checks its context file); give the skill a read-only context file and a verdict schema for its structured output; after it, upload the verdict for a script job to validate and act on, and the fix as a patch a prepare: apply-patch script pushes only on a fix verdict.

applied-by.description: What this read skill hands on, keyed by artifact, and the script activity that applies each: patch (its change to the tree, applied by a prepare: apply-patch script), feedback-replies, dependency-verdict, work-outcome. Only a skill with effect read and gating advisory sets it. The config reader rejects a target that is not a script, is not in every lane that holds the producer, or whose slot does not need the producer (README.md, Activities).

args.description: Arguments passed verbatim: after the skill name in that skill's own syntax, or to the script.

checks.description: Repository check scripts the skill may run, each with its fixed flags. The runner that stages the skill's edit tools (the write runner, or the read runner for a skill with applied-by.patch) runs each from the base copy against the checkout, through a wrapper the skill can call with no arguments.

self-checks.description: Advisory repository check scripts the skill runs and fixes before it hands its change on, each with its fixed flags, through the same wrapper as checks. Unlike checks, the runner never runs them again, so a failure the skill cannot fix still opens the PR and is named in its report.

verify-scripts.description: Exact repository-relative paths of scripts the skill may run with any arguments. The runner that stages the skill's edit tools copies each script's plugin (or the base scripts/) to a read-only directory, denies Edit and Write on it, and allows a wrapper that runs the script from the checkout, with GH_TOKEN and GITHUB_TOKEN unset (code it runs can still read the token from an ancestor process), with any arguments but a path outside it. A script that changes files, runs code from the checkout, or reaches the network hands the run that power: list one only when it limits itself, as scripts/run-test-file.sh, scripts/git-mv-rm.sh and scripts/new-changelog-fragment.sh do, or when the run may hold that power, as plugins/skill-quality/scripts/check-skill.sh (checkout test scripts and markdownlint) does.

web-access.description: Whether the skill may read the web, off when absent. On, the runner that stages the skill's edit tools allows WebSearch, WebFetch to the listed domains (`any`: every domain), and the research skills, and the listed domains also open to the skill's sandboxed shell commands. On needs reads-untrusted: true.

permission-mode.description: The Claude Code permission mode a PR-mode skill runs in on the read runner's launcher (run-claude-cli), dontAsk when absent. auto lets the auto-mode classifier approve tool calls no rule allows; the run job fails red unless the CLI's init message reports the mode asked for. Other runners run dontAsk whatever this says.

script.description: Repository-relative path of a scripted step with no model in it.

effect.description: What the activity may change. The runner derives ordering and the token grant from it and checks that a read activity left the tree clean, unless the activity hands its change on as a patch.

gating.description: A gate verdict feeds ci-status; an advisory verdict is reported only.

reads-untrusted.description: True when the activity reads text from issues, PR bodies, comments or web pages, or PR head files, which can quote such text.

needs.description: Activities in the same slots or children list that must finish first.

applies-when.description: Replaces the activity's predicate for this slot.

models.description: The model, effort and turn budget of every model run, as named profiles and a route from each run to one. A skill activity's route is its activity name; a run that is no activity takes a run route: verify-pr for pr-verify.yml, review-code and review-security for the code and security review lanes, triage-issue for intake triage, summarize-reuse for work-resolve-issue's summary of a reused lane branch. A run with no route takes default-profile. Absent: every run takes the built-in standard profile, model default with 75 turns (README.md, Models).

default-profile.description: The profile of every run no route names. Must be a key of profiles.

routes.description: Run -> profile. A key is a skill activity or a run route (verify-pr, review-code, review-security, triage-issue, summarize-reuse); a value is a key of profiles. The config reader rejects any other key or value.

issue-dimensions.description: The budget of a skill activity with input issue, from the issue's Size, Complexity and Uncertainty org issue fields, read by field and option id. A field with no value, or whose latest setter is neither a listed human nor the lanes App, reads as size small, complexity medium or uncertainty known, which the tables must define; an option no entry maps fails the resolve. The turn cap is the size's base-turns times the complexity factor, rounded up, and replaces the profile's max-turns (README.md, Models). The model step's timeout is the size's timeout-minutes less the minutes resolve-config keeps for saving a stopped run's work.

oneOf.description: Too big for one run: skips with split-required.

timeout-minutes.description: The run job's timeout-minutes, whatever the complexity. A run that outlasts it resumes in a new job from its lane branch.

complexity.description: Complexity -> the factor base-turns is multiplied by.

uncertainty.description: Uncertainty -> run, or the skip reason that sends the issue to research or a probe first.

complexity-profiles.description: Complexity -> the profile the run starts on, in place of its route's; a key is a key of complexity, a value a key of profiles. A complexity with no entry keeps the route's profile. The dimensions' turn cap still applies (README.md, Models).

field-id.description: The org issue field's id (REST issue_field_id).

options.description: Single-select option id -> the key of its table. A rename keeps the id.

profile.description: A model profile names its model, or a role profile names a multi-agent role, never both. A role profile has no model or effort key, so it can name neither default nor a model ID: its model and effort come from the role map, plugins/multi-agent/reference/defaults.yaml in the base checkout, and the model is opus when the role map gives inherit or no alias (README.md, Models).

model.description: A model alias, never a full model ID, passed as --model. default passes no --model, so the account's default model runs.

effort.description: Passed as --effort. Absent: no --effort, so the model's default effort applies.

role.description: The multi-agent role whose model the run takes.

workload.description: The role's workload, whose model and effort win over the role's own where the role map sets them.

effort-role.description: The role whose effort the run takes, in place of its own role's.

subagent-model.description: The model subagents run on when neither the spawn nor the agent definition names one, set as CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL through the run's settings. inherit sets nothing.

escalate-to.description: The profile one model rung up, a key of profiles, which a run resolved at model-rung 1 takes in place of this one. A run climbs at most one rung (README.md, Models).

merge.description: How far the repository's merge authority may merge without a human. A lane-power setting: raised only by a merged change to this file. Authority local-babysit requires an agent-identity and, at a rung above off, a diff-check with denied paths and a line cap; the pr-merge lane needs neither, and above off with an agent-identity it requires the verifier verdict.

rung.description: Highest work class the merge authority merges. C1 produces no PR; C4 and C5 need a human (README.md, Merge authority).

authority.description: The one lane that merges for this repository: the local babysit wrapper or the pr-merge lane. Absent means pr-merge, the meaning a rung had before this key existed; the babysit wrapper merges only when this names the authority it runs as (README.md, Merge authority).

report-only.description: true: the merge authority reports each decision and writes nothing (no enqueue, dequeue or comment). The pr-merge lane starts true; the owner sets false to let it merge (README.md, Merge authority).

lane-prs.description: How the agent identity's own pull requests merge. native: GitHub's auto-merge, armed by the enable-auto-merge activity and gated by ci-status; the pr-merge gate does not list, score or enqueue them. gate: the pr-merge gate lists, scores and enqueues them as well (README.md, Native auto-merge).

require-verifier-verdict.description: true: the pr-merge lane refuses a pull request, and dequeues a queued one, without a passing pr-verify verdict at its head (README.md, Verifier verdict). It is the lane's merge criterion, so an enabled pr-merge lane (agent-identity set) at a rung above off must set it true; the gate refuses `verifier-verdict-not-required` otherwise.

max-in-flight.description: Lane merges allowed in flight at once: the agent identity's merge-queue entries plus its merged pull requests the post-merge check has not verified. The gate reads it at the default branch head, not the pull request's base, and refuses `in-flight:` at this count. A post-merge failure charges every unverified lane merge whose commit the red run contains, and any charge demotes the rung.

gate-budget-minutes.description: Minutes the pr-merge workflow's gate loop runs before it starts no further candidate. The candidate in progress finishes, so no gate stops between its check and its enqueue; the next run starts after the last candidate reached. Keep it below the merge job's timeout-minutes less the longest single candidate. Absent: no budget.

gate-candidate-minutes.description: Minutes one candidate's gate may spend in its read phases (the merge policy, then the verdict). Past it the gate starts no further read command and reports the candidate unknown (exit 11, reason unknown:candidate-deadline), never ready; no write is bounded, so none is cut short. The loop goes on to the next candidate within gate-budget-minutes. The first candidate a run stops is gated first in the next run under gate-deferred-minutes, so one that always runs past it still gets a longer gate. Absent: no limit.

gate-deferred-minutes.description: Minutes the gate may read for the candidate the last run deferred at gate-candidate-minutes, gated first in its run; writes are never bounded, as there. A candidate stopped at this ceiling gets a warning annotation and goes back to the capped rotation, never deferred again. Keep it below the merge job's timeout-minutes less the closing steps. Absent: no limit.

skip-unchanged.description: The pr-merge workflow reports a candidate the last run refused on unchanged inputs with that refusal, marked carried, instead of gating it again; a skip only repeats a refusal (README.md, Merge authority). 0 in either key: no skips.

max-minutes.description: Minutes after a refusal was judged at which the candidate is gated again, unchanged or not.

max-skips.description: Runs in a row that may skip a candidate before one gates it again, unchanged or not.

max-queue-ejections.description: Merge-queue removals for failed checks since the pull request's head last changed (a pushed commit or a force push) at which the unattended merge gate stops enqueuing that head: the queue would eject it again on the same commits. A push resets the count.

quarantine-days.description: Days a quarantine issue excuses its suite's failures outside the merges' affected set from post-merge demotion, counted from when it was filed (README.md, The local babysit lane, Quarantined suites). At most 30, so a flaky suite goes no more than a month without its failures demoting again (judgment) and the date arithmetic stays in range; any other value is 7.

max-verify-fails.description: Counted pr-verify fail verdicts at this many distinct heads of one pull request refuse it `verify:repeated-fail`, for a human, whatever a later pass says (README.md, Verifier verdict). Any other value is 1, so any earlier fail holds.

risk-escalation-minutes.description: Minutes the agent identity's MED or HIGH reasons comment must have stood unchanged (same score, reasons and head), timed from its last change, before the unattended merge gate adds the tracker's human-gated role label. 0: no minimum, so the second run that finds the same comment labels it. A rewrite of the reasons restarts the time.

check-inputs.description: Git pathspecs of files the pull request checks read but a pull request rarely changes (a registry, an allowlist). When the base changed one since a pull request's merge base, the unattended merge gate updates its branch from the base (a merge, never a rebase) instead of enqueuing it, and enqueues the new head once its checks pass. `scripts/shared-copies.txt` counts only for a pull request whose own changes touch a path it registers. Empty or absent: nothing is updated.

verify-authors.description: Whose pull requests pr-verify.yml judges. lane: only those the lanes App (agent-identity, a Bot account) opened; lane-or-owner: those and the owner account's (a User matched by account id), whose idle pull requests the pr-merge lane adopts; any: every author's. The resolver skips on any other value (README.md, Verifier verdict).

agent-identity.description: GitHub login the unattended merge lane acts as. It must be the [bot] login of a GitHub App dedicated to this lane: a machine user is a User and would pass every human test, and GitHub's shared built-in bots (github-actions[bot], dependabot[bot]) are rejected in any letter case. Absent: the unattended path stays inert. Required when authority is local-babysit.

denied-paths.description: Globs a lane-merged diff may not touch. Empty: the pr-merge lane denies no path (README.md, The pr-merge lane).

max-changed-lines.description: Changed lines above which the diff scores MED. Absent: no cap in the pr-merge lane; the local babysit lane requires it.

max-changed-files.description: pr-merge lane only: changed files above which the diff scores MED. Absent: no cap. The local babysit lane always caps at 8.

high-path-floor.description: true scores a diff touching the risk scorer's fixed HIGH path floor (the trusted-actor list, the trusted-trigger check, code owners, submodules and resolve-config) HIGH, as it does a plugin or marketplace manifest change that installs or runs something new. Absent or false: only denied-paths count. The local babysit lane always applies the floor.

c2-contradictions.description: pr-merge lane only: true scores a C2 diff that removes, renames or copies a file, changes a schema, or spans plugins MED. Absent or false: not checked. The local babysit lane always checks.

dependabot.description: The pr-merge lane's Dependabot class: on verified Dependabot commits and a green ci-status, a tier auto pull request (every update non-major) merges, and a tier review one merges on the lanes App's verdict=merge marker at its head; no closing issue or denied-path rule (README.md, Dependabot pull requests).

mode.description: enforce: merge Dependabot pull requests whatever merge.report-only says. report: report each decision and write nothing. off: refuse every Dependabot pull request and leave them unlisted.

majors.description: hold: refuse a pull request with a major update, one whose version cannot be read, or one whose title and commit metadata disagree, whatever the review verdict says, and escalate it to a human with the tracker's human-gated role label. review: a major update is tier review and merges on the lanes App's verdict=merge marker.
